bundles.name: Value expression and numeric fidelity
bundles.description: The numeric side of the value object: what the number is bound to, what form it takes, and how its precision and exactness survive storage and transfer.
bundles.rationale: VIM 1.19 defines a quantity value as a number and a reference together; FHIR makes decimal precision semantically significant and adds a comparator for bounded results; ISO 80000-1 specifies rounding of numbers. Losing precision or splitting value from unit are the two most common silent failures in exchanged quantity data.

layers.name: Value composition and form
layers.description: How the number binds to its reference, and whether the value is a point, an interval, a bound or a ratio.

findings.name: Numeric value and reference binding
findings.description: VIM 1.19 defines a quantity value as a number and reference together, where the reference may be a measurement unit (5.34 m), a measurement procedure (43.5 HRC) or a reference material (5.0 IU/l). VIM 1.20 defines the numerical quantity value as the number in that expression. The number may be complex, and vector or tensor quantities have a value per component. The operational consequence is that value and reference form an atomic pair: neither may be written, updated, defaulted or indexed independently, and D-SI carries them as one payload with uncertainty.

questions.text: What is the numerical value, and which reference type does it bind to — unit, measurement procedure or reference material?
Is the numerical value real, complex, vector or tensor, and how are components carried and ordered?
Is the value/reference pair enforced as atomic, so that no write path can set one without the other?

data_elements.name: Numerical quantity value
data_elements.description: The number component of the quantity value, carried in a representation that preserves the source precision.

data_elements.name: Reference type
data_elements.description: Whether the reference is a measurement unit, a measurement procedure or a reference material.

data_elements.name: Vector or tensor components
data_elements.description: Ordered component values for a vector or tensor quantity, each a number sharing or overriding the parent reference.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This is the irreducible inline payload of the mixin. Externalising the number or reference into a separate artifact would break the atomicity the finding exists to enforce.

findings.name: Value forms, bounds and comparators
findings.description: A quantity value is not always a point. FHIR provides a comparator element (<, <=, >=, >, plus ad-hoc statistical markers) that modifies the meaning of the value, and separate Range and Ratio types; SimpleQuantity forbids the comparator. schema.org QuantitativeValue offers minValue and maxValue for intervals. Detection limits, censored values, values outside the measuring interval and rate expressions all need an explicit form so that a consumer never mistakes a bound for a point estimate.

questions.text: Is this value a point, a one-sided bound, an interval, or a ratio of two quantities?
answer_data: numerator and denominator quantities if a ratio

questions.text: For an interval, are the bounds inclusive, and must both bounds share the same unit?
How is a result below a detection limit or outside the measuring interval encoded so it is not aggregated as a point value?
Which value forms are prohibited in this property slot?

data_elements.name: Value form
data_elements.description: Whether the value is a point, bounded, interval, ratio or censored result.

data_elements.name: Comparator
data_elements.description: Operator that modifies the meaning of the numeric value when the true value is known only to be above or below it.

data_elements.name: Interval bounds
data_elements.description: Lower and upper bounds with explicit inclusivity, sharing the parent unit.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Value form, comparator and bounds are inline structural variants of the same embedded value object; no separately identified artifact is produced or exchanged.

layers.name: Numeric representation and fidelity
layers.description: How the number survives storage, serialisation and arithmetic without silent loss of meaning.

findings.name: Precision, rounding and exactness
findings.description: FHIR states that a Quantity value 'includes an implicit precision in the presentation of the value' and that 0.010 is regarded as different from 0.01, so trailing zeros are semantically significant and must be preserved. ISO 80000-1:2022 specifies rules for rounding of numbers, and NIST SP 811 gives rules for expressing values of quantities. Binary floating-point representation destroys both trailing-zero precision and exact decimal round-trips, so the representation choice is a semantic decision, not an implementation detail. Some values are exact by definition (the SI defining constants, and defined conversions such as 1 in = 25.4 mm) and must never be rounded.

questions.text: How many significant digits are meaningful, and are trailing zeros preserved through storage and serialisation?
Is this value exact by definition or an approximation subject to rounding?
answer_data: defining authority for an exact value

questions.text: Which numeric representation is mandated to guarantee lossless round-trip, and what is the behaviour if a consumer cannot honour it?
answer_data: mandated representation (decimal string, arbitrary precision decimal, rational)

questions.text: Which rounding rule applies when the value is scaled, converted or aggregated, and is the rounding recorded?

data_elements.name: Significant digits
data_elements.description: Number of digits in the value that carry measurement meaning, distinct from the digits used in storage.

data_elements.name: Exactness indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the value is exact by definition and must not be rounded, or is an approximation.

data_elements.name: Numeric representation form
data_elements.description: Declared representation used to carry the number without loss, for example arbitrary-precision decimal string or exact rational.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Precision and exactness are properties of the inline number itself. The only durable artifact in this area is the deployment's numeric-representation policy, which is governed under the service layers rather than duplicated as a finding artifact.

bundles.name: Comparability and conversion
bundles.description: When two quantity values may be compared, and how a value is transformed from one unit to another without silently corrupting its meaning.
bundles.rationale: UCUM defines commensurability as sharing a dimension while noting that commensurable units need not be equal, and separates proper units convertible by scalar factor from special units convertible only by function. QUDT supplies conversionMultiplier and conversionOffset, and its v3.4.0 release replaced ambiguous broader-than relations with an explicit commensurability framework — direct evidence that naive dimension matching is unsafe.

layers.name: Commensurability and comparison
layers.description: The tests that decide whether two values may lawfully be compared, added or aggregated.

findings.name: Commensurability, equality and comparison rules
findings.description: UCUM treats two units as commensurable when they share the same dimension, while stressing that commensurable units need not be equal, and that equality forms a narrower equivalence class than commensurability. Arbitrary units form no equivalence classes at all and are incomparable even to other arbitrary units. QUDT v3.4.0 introduced explicit relations such as qudt:specializationOf and qudt:unitForQuantityKind precisely because dimensional matching alone produced wrong equivalences. Comparison of values carrying uncertainty is a further distinct decision that must not default to bare numeric comparison.

questions.text: Are the two units commensurable, and by which test — equal dimension, equal quantity kind, or both?
answer_data: dimension and kind of each operand

questions.text: Does commensurability alone authorise comparison here, or is agreement on quantity kind also required?
How are equality and ordering defined when one or both values carry uncertainty or a comparator?
Which comparisons must be refused outright rather than approximated?
answer_data: prohibited comparison classes such as arbitrary-unit pairs

data_elements.name: Commensurability determination
data_elements.description: Recorded outcome of a commensurability test between two units, with the test kind and the vocabulary version used.

data_elements.name: Comparison semantics identifier
data_elements.description: Named rule set governing equality and ordering for values of this kind, including uncertainty handling.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A commensurability determination is a derived computation over pinned registry data; persisting it as an artifact would create a cache that silently ages when the registry version changes.

layers.name: Conversion mechanics and consequences
layers.description: The parameters and functions that convert values between units, and the provenance and loss that conversion creates.

findings.name: Linear and non-linear conversion
findings.description: QUDT expresses conversion as qudt:conversionMultiplier with an optional qudt:conversionOffset relative to the coherent SI unit of the kind. UCUM distinguishes proper units, where conversion factors derive from dimensional analysis over its base set (meter, second, gram, radian, kelvin, coulomb, candela), from special units on non-ratio scales such as degree Celsius, which require mathematical functions rather than scalar multiplication. The critical trap is that converting a point on an interval scale and converting a difference on the same scale use different rules: a temperature difference of 5 °C is 5 K, but a temperature of 5 °C is 278.15 K.

questions.text: What multiplier and offset convert this unit to the coherent SI unit of its quantity kind?
Does the unit require a non-linear conversion function rather than multiplier and offset?
Is this value a point on the scale or a difference, and which conversion rule therefore applies?
Which authority publishes the conversion factor, at what version, and is the factor exact or rounded?
answer_data: exact or rounded designation with digits

data_elements.name: Conversion multiplier
data_elements.description: Factor converting a value in this unit to the coherent SI unit of the same quantity kind.

data_elements.name: Conversion offset
data_elements.description: Additive offset applied after the multiplier for units on non-zero-origin scales.

data_elements.name: Conversion function reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and parameters of a non-linear conversion function required by a special unit.

data_elements.name: Point or difference designation
data_elements.description: Whether the value denotes a point on the scale or a difference, selecting whether the offset applies.

artifacts.name: Pinned conversion factor table
artifacts.description: The set of conversion multipliers, offsets and function references in force for a deployment, pinned to named authority editions so that a historical conversion can be reproduced exactly.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus monotonically increasing release number in the adopting Dimension namespace; each row cites its upstream authority document and edition.

findings.name: Conversion provenance and information loss
findings.description: Every conversion is a derivation that can lose information. A converted value that overwrites the original destroys the ability to audit or reverse the transformation, and rounding after conversion silently changes the implied precision. D-SI carries value, unit and uncertainty as a single payload precisely so that a transformed result remains metrologically interpretable. Round-trip conversion through binary floating point is frequently not idempotent.

questions.text: Is the stored value the value as originally reported, or a derivative produced by conversion?
What precision or uncertainty was lost in the conversion, and is the pre-conversion value retained?
Is the conversion reversible without drift, and is a round-trip check required before the result is accepted?

data_elements.name: Source quantity value
data_elements.description: The originally reported value and unit from which a converted value was derived.

data_elements.name: Conversion timestamp
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z recording when the conversion was performed.

data_elements.name: Conversion loss note
data_elements.description: Recorded statement of precision, uncertainty or scale information lost or approximated during conversion.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Conversion provenance is inline metadata attached to the derived value so it travels with it; separating it into an artifact would let a converted value circulate without its own derivation record.

bundles.name: Quality, uncertainty and validation
bundles.description: How confidence in the value is stated, how tolerance and conformity decisions are separated from measurement uncertainty, and how constraints and validation outcomes are recorded.
bundles.rationale: The GUM defines the normative vocabulary for stating uncertainty; VIM separates measurement uncertainty from tolerance. Conflating the two produces invalid conformity decisions. Constraint specification and explicit validation outcomes are what make a quantity value safe for automated consumption.

layers.name: Uncertainty and tolerance
layers.description: Stating dispersion attributable to measurement, and separately stating the permitted interval a value must fall within.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty expression
findings.description: The GUM defines standard uncertainty as the standard deviation characterising the dispersion of values attributable to the measurand, evaluated by Type A (statistical analysis of repeated observations) or Type B (other means such as certificates or expert judgement) methods, combined into a combined standard uncertainty and optionally multiplied by a coverage factor k to give an expanded uncertainty with a stated coverage probability. A reported uncertainty without its type, coverage factor and coverage probability is uninterpretable. D-SI carries these as structured fields alongside value and unit.

questions.text: Is the reported uncertainty a standard uncertainty, a combined standard uncertainty or an expanded uncertainty?
answer_data: unit of the uncertainty or relative flag

questions.text: For an expanded uncertainty, what coverage factor and coverage probability apply, and how was the factor chosen?
answer_data: basis for choosing k, including effective degrees of freedom if used

questions.text: Were the contributing components evaluated by Type A or Type B methods, and is the evidence for Type B components recorded?
answer_data: evidence reference for Type B components

questions.text: Is the uncertainty expressed in the same unit as the value or as a relative quantity, and how is that declared?
answer_data: conversion rule between the two forms

data_elements.name: Uncertainty value
data_elements.description: Numeric magnitude of the reported uncertainty, in the same unit as the value or declared relative.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty type
data_elements.description: Standard, combined standard or expanded uncertainty per GUM terminology.

data_elements.name: Coverage factor
data_elements.description: Numerical factor k relating expanded uncertainty to combined standard uncertainty.

data_elements.name: Coverage probability
data_elements.description: Stated probability that the interval defined by the expanded uncertainty contains the measurand value.

artifacts.name: Uncertainty budget
artifacts.description: Itemised statement of uncertainty components, their evaluation type, distributions, sensitivity coefficients and combination, substantiating the reported uncertainty. Referenced by the value rather than embedded in it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identifier issued by the originating laboratory or calibration system where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI minted by the adopting Dimension, always paired with the measurement it substantiates.

findings.name: Tolerance, specification limits and conformity decisions
findings.description: Tolerance is a requirement imposed by a specification; measurement uncertainty is a property of the measurement. They have different owners, different lifecycles and different consequences, and must never be stored in the same field. A conformity decision — whether the value passes — depends additionally on a decision rule and any guard band, and is a separate assertion from either the value or its uncertainty.

questions.text: What tolerance or specification interval applies to this value, and which authority set it?
answer_data: lower and upper specification limits with inclusivity

questions.text: Is a conformity decision recorded, and what decision rule and guard band produced it?
answer_data: guard band applied and its basis

questions.text: How does the record keep tolerance distinct from measurement uncertainty so neither is mistaken for the other?

data_elements.name: Specification limits
data_elements.description: Lower and upper permitted values with inclusivity, expressed in the same unit as the value.

data_elements.name: Conformity outcome
data_elements.description: Recorded pass, fail or indeterminate decision against the specification limits.

data_elements.name: Decision rule reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the decision rule, including any guard band, used to reach the conformity outcome.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The specification document that sets a tolerance belongs to a requirements or specification sibling model; this mixin carries only the limits in force and a reference to that document, so no artifact is produced here.

findings.name: Metrological traceability and evidence
findings.description: VIM defines metrological traceability as a property of a measurement result whereby the result can be related to a reference through a documented unbroken chain of calibrations, each contributing to the measurement uncertainty. ISO 11240 requires units used in medicinal-product interchange to be traceable to international metrological standards and provides mapping structures among vocabularies. After 20 May 2019 the SI reference is the set of defining constants rather than artefacts such as the international prototype of the kilogram. Claims of traceability without a chain are not conformance.

questions.text: To which international reference is this quantity value or unit claimed to be traceable, and is the calibration chain documented end to end?
What evidence artefacts support the traceability claim, such as a calibration certificate identifier, mise en pratique citation, or mapping table version?
Which organisation is responsible for maintaining the traceability claim, and under which accreditation or metrological authority?
Where does the chain stop, and is the result therefore only internally consistent rather than metrologically traceable?

data_elements.name: Traceability reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an SI defining constant, a national standard, or another stated metrological reference.

data_elements.name: Calibration chain documented
data_elements.description: True when an unbroken documented chain exists.

data_elements.name: Calibration certificate identifier
data_elements.description: Master identifier of a calibration certificate when one exists. Digital calibration certificate formats are an evidence gap if not supplied.

data_elements.name: Responsible organisation
data_elements.description: Organisation accountable for the traceability statement.

artifacts.name: Traceability record
artifacts.description: Documented chain from the quantity value or unit to a stated international reference, including certificate identifiers and mapping versions.
media_or_form: XML DCC if provided by host
artifacts.identity_strategy: Certificate or chain master identifier from the issuing metrology body; Dimension UUID only as a local surrogate.

layers.name: Constraint specification and validation
layers.description: The declarative constraints applied to a quantity slot and the recorded outcome of applying them.

findings.name: Constraints, validation outcomes and exception handling
findings.description: FHIR binds units through value sets on Quantity elements and restricts SimpleQuantity by forbidding a comparator; QUDT constrains admissible units per quantity kind through qudt:applicableUnit; UCUM conformance level determines whether an unrecognised expression can even be evaluated. A quantity slot needs a declared constraint set (allowed units, allowed value forms, plausibility range, cardinality, requiredness) and a recorded, re-evaluable validation outcome — because a value that passed under one registry release may fail under the next.

questions.text: Which units and value forms are permitted for this quantity slot, and with what binding strength?
answer_data: allowed unit value set and version

questions.text: What plausibility range, cardinality and requiredness apply, and are they hard constraints or advisory warnings?
answer_data: hard or advisory severity per rule

questions.text: What must a consumer do when the unit is unrecognised or a constraint fails — reject, quarantine, or accept with a flag?
Is the validation outcome persisted, and is it re-evaluated when the bound registry release changes?
answer_data: registry release the outcome was computed against

data_elements.name: Allowed unit value set
data_elements.description: Bound set of admissible unit codes for the slot, with the value set version and binding strength.

data_elements.name: Plausibility range
data_elements.description: Advisory lower and upper bounds used to detect implausible values without asserting a specification limit.

data_elements.name: Validation status
data_elements.description: Recorded outcome of constraint evaluation, with severity, rule identifiers and the registry release evaluated against.

artifacts.name: Quantity validation report
artifacts.description: Machine-readable record of constraint evaluation over a batch or stream of quantity values, listing rule identifiers, severities, failing values, the pinned registry and value set versions used, and the disposition applied.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI in the adopting Dimension namespace keyed by validation run, carrying an RFC 3339 run timestamp and the pinned registry release identifiers.

bundles.name: Context, provenance and lifecycle
bundles.description: The qualifiers that change how the same number and unit must be read, where the value came from, when it applies, and how it and its unit definitions change over time.
bundles.rationale: VIM 1.19 shows the reference may be a procedure or reference material, implying context-dependence; schema.org provides valueReference for exactly this; RFC 3339 fixes timestamp form; QUDT release history proves unit vocabularies change in breaking ways, so values must be pinned to the definitions in force when recorded.

layers.name: Contextual qualification
layers.description: Reference conditions, denominators and other qualifiers without which the number and unit are ambiguous.

findings.name: Reference conditions and denominator context
findings.description: The same number and unit can mean different things depending on context that is not encoded in either. Gas volumes depend on reference temperature and pressure; concentrations depend on the basis (dry weight, wet weight, per volume of what); rates depend on their denominator population and period; fuel consumption in L/100 km carries an implied per-distance basis. schema.org provides valueReference explicitly to carry such context, and unitText as a fallback where no code exists for compound expressions like 'L/100 km'. UCUM annotations can carry the denominator hint but are semantically void and discarded by conformant parsers, so they cannot be relied on for meaning.

questions.text: Under which reference conditions is this value defined, and are those conditions recorded as structured data rather than free text?
answer_data: reference temperature, pressure or other conditions as quantity values
basis code such as dry or wet weight

questions.text: For a rate or ratio, what is the denominator — per what entity, per what population, per what period?
Does a contextual qualifier change how the same number and unit must be interpreted, and is a consumer required to fail if it cannot interpret the qualifier?
Is any semantic meaning being carried in a UCUM annotation that a conformant parser will discard?
answer_data: structured relocation target for that meaning

data_elements.name: Reference conditions
data_elements.description: Structured conditions under which the value is defined, each itself a quantity value using this mixin.

data_elements.name: Denominator context
data_elements.description: Definition of the denominator entity, population or period for a rate or ratio value.

data_elements.name: Value reference qualifier
data_elements.description: Reference to a further structured value that qualifies interpretation, equivalent in role to schema.org valueReference.

artifacts.name: Reference condition definition record
artifacts.description: Named, versioned definition of a set of reference conditions (for example a standard temperature and pressure basis) that many values cite, so the basis can be revised without silently reinterpreting historical values.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative identifier from the defining standards body where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI in the adopting Dimension namespace with an explicit version.

layers.name: Provenance and time
layers.description: Where the value came from, by what means, and the separate times at which the phenomenon occurred and the value was recorded.

findings.name: Value origin and derivation
findings.description: Whether a value was measured, computed, estimated, asserted, defaulted or converted determines what may be inferred from it. SOSA distinguishes the observation act from its result and delegates the result's encoding; the mixin therefore carries a compact origin statement plus a reference to the fuller observation or calculation record in the sibling model. VIM 2.41 metrological traceability is a claim requiring an unbroken documented calibration chain, so it must be recorded as a referenced claim with evidence, never asserted by default.

questions.text: Was this value measured, computed, estimated, asserted, defaulted or converted?
answer_data: reference to the observation or calculation record

questions.text: If computed, from which input quantity values and by which documented method or expression?
answer_data: method or expression identifier and version

questions.text: Is a metrological traceability claim made, and what documented calibration evidence supports it?

data_elements.name: Origin category
data_elements.description: How the value came into existence: measured, computed, estimated, asserted, defaulted or converted.

data_elements.name: Originating agent
data_elements.description: Identifier of the person, device, service or model that produced the value.

data_elements.name: Traceability claim reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the calibration or reference-standard evidence supporting a metrological traceability claim.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Provenance here is a compact inline pointer set. The substantive artifacts — observation records, calculation specifications and calibration certificates — are owned by sibling models and referenced by identifier, so duplicating them here would fork the record of truth.

findings.name: Event time versus observation and record time
findings.description: A quantity value has at least two distinct times: when the phenomenon it describes occurred or held, and when the value was observed, ingested or recorded. Conflating them makes late-arriving data, backfills and corrections indistinguishable from real change. RFC 3339 fixes the format: seconds are required and an offset must be present, with 'Z' meaning UTC and '-00:00' explicitly meaning that UTC is known but the local offset is not — a distinction that must be preserved rather than normalised away.

questions.text: When did the phenomenon the value describes occur or hold, and when was the value observed or ingested?
Are both timestamps RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and is '-00:00' preserved where the local offset is unknown?
Over what interval is the value valid, and does it expire or require refresh?
How is a late-arriving or backfilled value distinguished from a genuine change in the measured quantity?

data_elements.name: Event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp, with seconds and explicit offset or Z, for when the described phenomenon occurred or held.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp for when the value was observed, received or recorded by the holding system.

data_elements.name: Validity interval
data_elements.description: Interval over which the value is asserted to hold, with explicit start and end or an open end.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Timestamps are inline attributes of the value record. Calendar and interval semantics beyond the RFC 3339 lexical form belong to the temporal sibling model and are referenced rather than restated.

layers.name: Versioning, deprecation and correction
layers.description: How changes to unit definitions and to recorded values are handled without retroactively falsifying history.

findings.name: Registry versioning, deprecation and value correction
findings.description: Unit vocabularies change in ways that alter meaning: QUDT v3.4.0 replaced ambiguous broader-than relations with an explicit commensurability framework and v3.5.0 redefined BIT, BYTE and OCTET as counting units; CGPM 2022 extended the prefix set; UN/CEFACT Rec 20 has reached Revision 17; the SI itself was redefined in 2019 in terms of exact defining constants. Values must therefore record the registry release in force when they were created, and the model must state whether historical values are reinterpreted under new definitions or frozen. Separately, a corrected value needs an explicit disposition — in-place amendment, superseding version, or retraction — because silent overwrite destroys auditability.

questions.text: Which registry release supplied the unit definition in force when this value was created?
Has the unit code since been deprecated, redefined or reclassified, and what is the successor and migration rule?
answer_data: migration rule and whether it is value-affecting

questions.text: Are historical values reinterpreted under a new unit definition, or frozen at the version of record?
When a value is corrected, is it amended in place, superseded by a new version, or retracted — and what remains visible?
answer_data: visibility of the prior value and its reason

data_elements.name: Registry release pin
data_elements.description: Identifier and release tag of each unit or quantity-kind registry release the value was resolved against.

data_elements.name: Unit lifecycle status
data_elements.description: Status of the unit code in its registry: active, deprecated, redefined, withdrawn, or replaced.

data_elements.name: Correction disposition
data_elements.description: How a change to a recorded value was applied: amended, superseded or retracted, with a reason code.

artifacts.name: Pinned registry release manifest
artifacts.description: Manifest listing every external unit, quantity-kind and value-set release the deployment has pinned, with release tags, retrieval timestamps, content digests and the breaking changes noted between releases.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus monotonically increasing manifest sequence number; each entry keyed by upstream registry URI, release tag and content digest.

artifacts.name: Unit deprecation and migration notice
artifacts.description: Notice issued when a pinned unit code is deprecated or redefined upstream, stating the successor code, whether the change is value-affecting, the affected value population and the remediation deadline.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI with a sequential notice number, carrying an RFC 3339 issue timestamp and references to the affected registry release manifest entries.

bundles.name: Interoperability, embedding and disclosure
bundles.description: How this mixin aligns with external standards without over-claiming conformance, how it is bound into exchanges, how it embeds in host records, and what access and retention rules attach to the values it carries.
bundles.rationale: Multiple credible unit vocabularies exist with genuine conflicts — schema.org places currency codes in unitCode, UCUM conformance levels change equality semantics, QUDT and UCUM have diverged on information units. Alignment must be recorded as alignment with strength and conflicts, never as conformance without evidence.

layers.name: External alignment and binding
layers.description: Recorded mappings to external vocabularies with strength and conflicts, and the profile bindings that govern a given exchange.

findings.name: Standard alignment and conflict register
findings.description: This model aligns to, and does not subsume, UCUM (machine grammar), UN/CEFACT Rec 20 (trade common codes), QUDT (IRIs, dimensions and conversion parameters), ISO 80000 and the SI Brochure (normative quantity and unit semantics), FHIR (a deployed binding) and schema.org (a web projection). Real conflicts must be registered rather than smoothed over: schema.org documents currency codes in unitCode although a currency has no quantity dimension; QUDT reclassified information units between releases; UCUM full versus limited conformance changes whether 'km' equals '1000.m'; and NIST SP 811 remains at its 2008 edition, predating the 2019 SI revision.

questions.text: To which external vocabularies is this unit or quantity kind aligned, and is each mapping exact, broader, narrower or approximate?
Where do the aligned standards conflict, and what resolution has been recorded for this deployment?
answer_data: standards in conflict with clause references

questions.text: Is conformance to a named standard being claimed, and what evidence substantiates the claim?
answer_data: scope and limits of the claim

questions.text: Which alignments are advisory only and must not be used to drive automated conversion?

data_elements.name: Alignment mapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from a local unit or quantity kind to an external vocabulary term, with target version, mapping strength and direction.

data_elements.name: Conformance claim
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of conformance to a named standard clause, with supporting evidence and stated scope limits.

artifacts.name: Alignment and conflict register
artifacts.description: Maintained register of every external alignment with its strength and pinned target version, alongside a dated list of known conflicts between aligned standards and the resolution adopted for each.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI in the adopting Dimension namespace, versioned by release; each row keyed by local term identifier plus target vocabulary URI and version.

findings.name: Profile binding and exchange negotiation
findings.description: A generic Quantity is rarely safe on the wire; it is made safe by a profile. FHIR demonstrates this with SimpleQuantity forbidding a comparator, with unit value-set bindings on specific elements, and with typed profiles (Age, Duration, Count, Distance, MoneyQuantity). An exchange must therefore state which profile applies, which value set binds the unit, the binding strength, and what happens when a partner sends something outside it — including whether the receiver fails closed or accepts with a flag.

questions.text: Which profile and unit value set bind this quantity slot in this exchange, and at what binding strength?
How was the binding agreed with the exchange partner, and where is that agreement recorded?
What is the receiver's behaviour when a value arrives outside the bound value set or violates the profile?

data_elements.name: Profile identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the profile constraining the quantity slot in a given exchange.

data_elements.name: Binding strength
data_elements.description: Whether the bound unit value set is required, extensible, preferred or example.

data_elements.name: Non-conformance disposition
data_elements.description: Declared receiver behaviour for values outside the bound value set or profile.

artifacts.name: Profile and value-set binding declaration
artifacts.description: Machine-readable declaration of the profiles, unit value sets, binding strengths and non-conformance dispositions in force for a named exchange, with effective dates.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus version in the adopting Dimension namespace; where an interoperability framework already issues canonical profile URLs, that identifier is authoritative.

layers.name: Embedding and disclosure
layers.description: How the mixin attaches to host records and what the host must decide about access, disclosure and retention of the values it carries.

findings.name: Mixin embedding contract
findings.description: The registry marks this model as an EMBED value object. Embedding rather than referencing means the quantity has no independent identity or lifecycle: it is created, versioned, secured and deleted with its host. FHIR's Quantity is a datatype, not a resource, for the same reason, and SOSA delegates result encoding to whatever vocabulary the host adopts. The contract must state the minimum field set every embedding carries, which host responsibilities are inherited rather than restated, and the narrow conditions under which a quantity may instead be referenced by identifier — for example a shared reference condition or a defining constant reused across many records.

questions.text: Is the quantity embedded as a value object in the host record, or referenced by identifier, and what justifies the choice?
Which fields are mandatory in every embedding, and which are conditionally required by scale type or origin?
Does the embedded quantity inherit the host record's identity, versioning and audit trail, or does it carry its own?
Which host-model responsibilities are explicitly delegated so this mixin does not restate them?

data_elements.name: Embedding mode
data_elements.description: Whether the quantity is embedded in the host record or referenced by identifier.

data_elements.name: Mandatory field set
data_elements.description: The minimum fields that must be present in any embedding for the value to be interpretable.

data_elements.name: Host record reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the record that owns the embedded quantity and from which it inherits identity and lifecycle.

artifacts.name: Embedding conformance profile
artifacts.description: Declaration of the mandatory and conditional field set for embeddings of this mixin in a given host model, with the inherited-responsibility list and worked minimal examples in at least one concrete projection.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus version in the adopting Dimension namespace, keyed by host model identifier and mixin version.

findings.name: Access, disclosure and retention of quantity values
findings.description: A quantity value is small but not neutral. Precise numeric values can re-identify individuals, reveal protected attributes, or disclose commercially sensitive process parameters, and precision reduction or banding is a recognised disclosure control that itself changes the value's meaning and must be recorded as a derivation. No consulted primary metrology or units standard addresses access control or retention for quantity values, so these rules are inherited from the host model and from the adopting Dimension's policy — this finding exists to make that delegation explicit and auditable rather than implicit.

questions.text: Can this numeric value, alone or combined with others, re-identify a person or reveal a controlled attribute?
Which access rule applies to the numeric value as against its unit and quantity-kind metadata?
Under which retention rule is the value deleted, and is the unit and provenance metadata retained so remaining data stays interpretable?
answer_data: deletion scope (value only or whole embedding)

questions.text: Is precision reduction, banding or perturbation applied as a disclosure control, and is that transformation recorded as provenance?
answer_data: recorded derivation from the original value

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Classification of the value's disclosure sensitivity, assigned by the host model's policy.

data_elements.name: Retention rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the retention rule governing the value, including trigger, period and deletion scope.

data_elements.name: Disclosure control applied
data_elements.description: Record of any precision reduction, banding or perturbation applied to the value before release, with parameters.

artifacts.name: Disclosure and retention policy record
artifacts.description: Policy record binding sensitivity classifications to access rules, retention periods, deletion scope and permitted disclosure-control techniques for quantity values in a given Dimension, with effective dates and approving authority.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed IRI plus version in the adopting Dimension namespace; where an enterprise policy register issues authoritative identifiers, that identifier takes precedence.

functions.name: Resolve unit reference
functions.description: Resolve a unit code, expression or display string to a pinned registry entry yielding the canonical expression, quantity kind, dimension vector, system membership and conversion parameters.
inputs: unit code or expression as received
code system URI and pinned version
preconditions: A registry release is pinned and retrievable
The parser conformance level is declared
effects: Records the registry release and resolution timestamp against the value
Raises an unresolved-unit exception with the declared disposition when no entry matches

functions.name: Parse and canonicalise unit expression
functions.description: Parse a compound unit expression under the pinned grammar, discard curly-brace annotations for semantic purposes, and emit a deterministic canonical form for equality and commensurability testing.
preconditions: Expression is in the character set the grammar admits
Conformance level is full where semantic equality is required
effects: Preserves the verbatim source expression alongside the canonical form
Rejects or quarantines unparseable expressions per the declared disposition

functions.name: Check commensurability and comparability
functions.description: Determine whether two quantity values may lawfully be compared, added or aggregated, testing dimension equality, quantity-kind agreement and scale-type compatibility, and refusing arbitrary-unit pairs outright.
outputs: comparability determination with the test applied
preconditions: Both units resolved against the same pinned registry release
Scale types are known for both operands
effects: Blocks the downstream operation when comparability fails
Emits a diagnostic naming the failing test

functions.name: Convert quantity value
functions.description: Convert a value to a target unit using the pinned multiplier and offset, or a declared non-linear function for special units, applying the point-versus-difference rule and recording the derivation.
preconditions: Source and target are commensurable and of the same quantity kind
Conversion parameters are pinned to a named authority edition
Scale type permits the requested conversion
effects: Retains the source value and unit as provenance
Suppresses the offset when converting a difference on an interval scale
Refuses conversion for arbitrary and procedure-defined units

functions.name: Normalise to coherent SI unit
functions.description: Express a value in the coherent SI unit of its quantity kind to give a canonical comparison basis, without discarding the value as originally reported.
inputs: coherent SI unit for the quantity kind
preconditions: Quantity kind is resolved
A coherent SI unit exists for the kind
effects: Stores the normalised value as a derived companion rather than replacing the original
Flags kinds with no coherent SI unit for manual handling

functions.name: Validate quantity value
functions.description: Evaluate a quantity value against its bound unit value set, permitted value forms, plausibility range, cardinality, requiredness and scale-type operation restrictions, and record a re-evaluable outcome.
inputs: profile and bound value set with versions
outputs: validation status with severity per rule
pinned versions the outcome was computed against
preconditions: Unit is resolved or an explicit unresolved disposition exists
Binding strength is declared
effects: Applies the declared disposition on failure: reject, quarantine or accept with a flag
Marks the outcome stale when a pinned registry release changes

functions.name: Assert measurement uncertainty
functions.description: Attach a GUM-conformant uncertainty statement to a value, requiring the uncertainty type and, for expanded uncertainty, the coverage factor and coverage probability.
inputs: coverage factor and coverage probability where expanded
outputs: reference to the substantiating uncertainty budget
preconditions: Uncertainty is expressed in the value's unit or explicitly declared relative
Uncertainty type is one of standard, combined standard or expanded
effects: Rejects an expanded uncertainty lacking a coverage factor or coverage probability
Links the value to the uncertainty budget artifact when one exists

functions.name: Decide conformity against specification
functions.description: Compare a value and its uncertainty against specification limits using a named decision rule and any guard band, and record the outcome separately from both the value and its uncertainty.
outputs: decision record citing rule and guard band
preconditions: Specification limits share the value's unit
Decision rule is named and versioned
effects: Writes the conformity outcome as a distinct assertion, never overwriting the value
Returns indeterminate rather than pass or fail when uncertainty straddles a limit under the rule

functions.name: Render quantity for presentation
functions.description: Produce a locale-appropriate display string from the resolved unit and the value's significant digits, applying the pinned style authority's printing and spelling rules without mutating the stored value.
preconditions: Significant digits are known or a default digit policy is declared
Style authority edition is pinned
effects: Leaves the stored numeric value and unit code unchanged
Marks the display string as non-authoritative and non-parseable

functions.name: Reconcile pinned registry release
functions.description: Compare a newly published unit or quantity-kind registry release against the pinned manifest, classify each change as cosmetic, semantic or value-affecting, and issue migration notices for affected values.
preconditions: The current manifest records release tags and content digests
Affected value populations are queryable by unit code
effects: Blocks silent adoption of value-affecting changes
Triggers re-validation of values whose bound registry release changed
Records the reconciliation with an RFC 3339 timestamp

functions.name: Record value provenance and times
functions.description: Attach the origin category, originating agent, derivation inputs and both event time and observation/ingestion time to a quantity value in RFC 3339 form with explicit offsets.
outputs: supersession link where the value replaces an earlier one
preconditions: Timestamps carry seconds and an explicit offset or Z
Origin category is from the declared vocabulary
effects: Preserves '-00:00' where the local offset is genuinely unknown
Distinguishes backfilled values from genuine change by comparing event and observation times

functions.name: Apply quantity calculus
functions.description: Multiply, divide, exponentiate, add or subtract quantity values under dimensional homogeneity and coherent-factor accounting.
preconditions: Addition and subtraction require same kind, not only same dimension.
Operands are not arbitrary units unless the operation is explicitly local to that assay.
effects: Produces a derived quantity value.
Fails closed on homogeneity violations.

functions.name: Map unit code
functions.description: Translate a unit identifier from one vocabulary to another using an authorised crosswalk, recording mapping type and conflicts.
preconditions: Crosswalk version is in force.
Currency codes are not mapped into SI units.
effects: Returns unmatched rather than inventing an equivalent.
Surfaces recorded non-isomorphisms such as UCUM versus SI angle.

functions.name: Freeze original quantity value
functions.description: Create an immutable snapshot of the originally recorded lexical value, unit, comparator and provenance before any conversion.
preconditions: A host master identifier exists or the Dimension assigns a UUID.
Event time and ingestion time are recorded separately when known.
effects: Makes the original lexical form indelible for the host retention period.
Subsequent conversions reference the snapshot rather than overwriting it.

composition.purpose: The observation act supplies the context in which a quantity value is a result; SOSA explicitly defines no units and delegates their encoding, so this mixin fills that slot and references the observation rather than restating sensor, procedure or feature of interest.
Event time, observation time and validity intervals are carried here in RFC 3339 lexical form, but calendar, interval, recurrence and timezone-rule semantics are owned by the temporal sibling.
Origin category, originating agent, derivation inputs and supersession links are provenance concerns mixed into the quantity value object rather than modelled independently within it.
Traceability claims and uncertainty budgets referenced from a quantity value are substantiated by calibration chains, reference standards and certificates owned by that model.

Monetary amounts share the numeric-fidelity and value-form rules but have no quantity dimension; a currency code must resolve through the Money model even where a projection such as schema.org places it in unitCode.
Lengths, areas, volumes and angles used in geometry are quantity values from this mixin, but coordinates, coordinate reference systems and datum transformations belong to the spatial model.
Unit code lists are consumed and pinned here; their publication cadence, deprecation policy and issuance governance belong to the registry sibling.

composition.target: UCUM — The Unified Code for Units of Measure v2.2
composition.purpose: Alignment for machine-parseable unit expressions, prefix and atom rules, annotation handling, special and arbitrary unit semantics, commensurability and conformance levels. Alignment, not conformance: conformance requires a tested parser declaration.
Alignment for three-character common codes required in trade and supply-chain exchange, crosswalked to UCUM expressions and QUDT IRIs with explicit mapping strength.

Alignment for unit and quantity-kind IRIs, dimension vectors, conversion multiplier and offset, applicable-unit constraints and the commensurability framework, pinned by release because QUDT has made value-affecting changes between releases.

composition.target: ISO 80000 series / ISQ and the SI Brochure
composition.purpose: Normative alignment for the system of quantities, dimensions, coherent units, prefixes, printing rules, rounding and logarithmic quantities. Full ISO 80000 text is paywalled, so clause-level conformance is not claimed.
Alignment for the uncertainty vocabulary and reporting requirements: standard, combined standard and expanded uncertainty, Type A and Type B evaluation, coverage factor and coverage probability.

Alignment to a widely deployed concrete binding covering value, comparator, unit, system and code, decimal precision significance, and profiled variants; used as an interoperability test case rather than as the model's semantics.
Alignment to the web projection using UN/CEFACT unitCode, unitText fallback, minValue/maxValue and valueReference, with the currency-in-unitCode divergence recorded as a conflict.

composition.target: D-SI SmartCom XML exchange format v2.2.0
composition.purpose: Alignment to a metrology-native exchange format that carries value, unit and uncertainty as one payload, used to test that this mixin's mandatory field set is sufficient for metrological round-tripping.

owner_package_requirements: Name a single accountable owner for the model instance in the adopting Dimension, with a named deputy, since the registry entry currently records only 'owner designated by the adopting Dimension'.
Maintain the pinned registry release manifest for every external unit, quantity-kind and value-set vocabulary in use, including release tags, retrieval timestamps and content digests.
Publish and version the alignment and conflict register, the unit code crosswalk and the conversion factor table, and review them whenever an upstream release is reconciled.
Declare the deployment's UCUM parser conformance level and the numeric representation policy, and test both against a published corpus before adoption.
Operate a change-notification path to consumers for value-affecting unit changes, with a stated remediation deadline.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable namespace under the adopting Dimension for locally minted terms, for example {dimension-base}/xct/qty/. Never mint a local identifier where a governed one exists: prefer the upstream unit IRI, then the UCUM expression, then the UN/CEFACT common code. Local extension codes must be namespaced so they can never be mistaken for a governed code, must carry an explicit 'local' marker, and must be reviewed for retirement whenever an upstream release adds the missing term.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-xct-008 (WM-XCT-008, entry kind mixin, validation flag: EMBED value object)
UCUM specification and unit atom tables (https://ucum.org/ucum)
QUDT unit and quantity-kind vocabularies, pinned by release (https://github.com/qudt/qudt-public-repo/releases)
BIPM SI Brochure and CGPM resolutions for base units, coherent derived units and prefixes (https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure)

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalise the unit expression under the pinned grammar with a deterministic operator, exponent and factor ordering; retain the verbatim source expression alongside it and never discard the original.
Discard curly-brace annotations before any semantic comparison, but retain their text in a separate annotation field so nothing is silently lost.

Preserve the numeric value as an exact decimal lexical form including trailing zeros; canonicalisation must never renormalise 0.010 to 0.01, and must never route the value through binary floating point.
Normalise timestamps to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, preserving '-00:00' where the local offset is genuinely unknown rather than rewriting it to Z.
Compute derived data — dimension vector, coherent-SI normalised value, commensurability determinations — on demand from the pinned registry rather than persisting it as canonical.
patch_rules: A patch may never modify the numeric value or the unit independently; the value and its reference are a single atomic unit of change.
Any change that alters the interpreted magnitude — unit change, precision change, conversion, rounding — is value-affecting and requires a new version with provenance, not an in-place amendment.
Adding provenance, alignment, annotation or validation-outcome fields is non-value-affecting and may be applied in place with an audit entry.
A correction must declare its disposition — amended, superseded or retracted — and retain the prior value with a reason code; silent overwrite is prohibited.
Patches that adopt a new upstream registry release must be preceded by a reconciliation that classifies every change as cosmetic, semantic or value-affecting.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional field, an alignment or a new alternate code is backward compatible.
Narrowing a binding, tightening a constraint, changing a binding strength to required, or changing the mandatory field set is breaking and requires a major version and consumer notification.

Redefining or reclassifying a unit code upstream is breaking for values already recorded against it; historical values remain frozen at their recorded registry release unless a documented reinterpretation decision states otherwise.
Consumers must fail closed on an unrecognised required field and must not infer a unit from a display string under any circumstances.
A conformance claim to any external standard is valid only with cited evidence and a stated scope; alignment alone never implies conformance.

identity_priority: Identifier issued by the authoritative master system or defining standards body — for example an upstream unit registry IRI, a UN/CEFACT common code, or a laboratory-issued uncertainty budget identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI minted in the adopting Dimension namespace where no authoritative identifier exists, always paired with an explicit version.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension as a last resort, recorded alongside any natural keys rather than replacing them.
A date, a release year, a display string or a unit symbol is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or 'Z'; event time and observation/ingestion time are recorded in separate fields and never collapsed. '-00:00' is preserved where UTC is known but the local offset is not, and is not rewritten to 'Z'.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Artifacts marked serial — the pinned registry release manifest, deprecation and migration notices, and the conversion factor table — carry a monotonically increasing sequence number within a stable governed IRI base, with no gaps and no reuse; each issue records an RFC 3339 issue timestamp and the sequence numbers it supersedes.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every pinned external artifact records a content digest and retrieval timestamp so a historical resolution can be reproduced exactly; any artifact whose digest no longer matches its upstream source is marked drifted, blocked from automated conversion use, and referred for reconciliation before adoption.

policies: Value and unit are inseparable: no interface may expose, accept, index or persist a numeric value without its resolved reference, and no default unit may ever be inferred.
Alignment is not conformance: external standards are recorded as alignments with mapping strength and pinned target versions, and a conformance claim requires cited evidence and a stated scope.
Registry releases are pinned, never floating: every value records the unit and quantity-kind releases it was resolved against, and upstream releases are adopted only after change classification.
Precision is semantic: trailing zeros, significant digits and exactness flags are preserved end to end, and any rounding, banding or precision reduction is recorded as a derivation with provenance.
Refuse rather than approximate: comparison or conversion involving arbitrary units, incompatible scale types or unresolved units is refused with a diagnostic, not silently coerced.
Access, retention and deletion rules are inherited from the host record and the adopting Dimension's policy; this mixin records the inheritance explicitly and asserts no independent rules.
Unknown or unmapped inbound units are not converted; they follow the Dimension unknown-unit action of reject, store-text or queue-for-steward.
Original recorded quantity values are retained at least as long as the host record and are not overwritten by canonicalised forms.
Unit definitions are deprecated, not deleted, so historical values remain interpretable.
Currency, calendar instants, geometry and units of presentation are out of scope and must be refused or redirected to sibling models.
Uncertainty, when required by the host measurement context, uses GUM terms and a unit commensurable with the value.

read: Read returns the numeric value together with its resolved reference, scale type and the pinned registry releases used for resolution; a value-only read is not offered.
Derived views — coherent-SI normalisation, display rendering, dimension vector — are computed at read time from the pinned registry and labelled as derived.
Reads that cross a sensitivity boundary apply the host record's access rule and record the disclosure control applied, if any.
create: Create requires the mandatory embedding field set, a resolvable reference or an explicit unresolved-unit disposition, and both event time and observation time where the host model demands them.
On create, the unit is resolved against the pinned registry release and that release identifier is written to the value.
Creation of a value whose unit fails resolution follows the declared disposition — reject, quarantine or accept with a flag — and is never silently defaulted.
update: Value-affecting updates create a new version with provenance linking to the prior value; the value and reference are updated atomically or not at all.
Non-value-affecting updates — provenance enrichment, alignment additions, validation-outcome refresh — are applied in place with an audit entry.
Bulk updates driven by a registry release change require a completed reconciliation and an issued migration notice before execution.
delete: Deletion is governed by the host record's retention rule; an embedded value has no independent deletion lifecycle.
Where a value is deleted but its context must remain interpretable, the unit, quantity kind and provenance metadata may be retained under an explicit policy decision and the deletion recorded.
Retraction of an erroneous value preserves a tombstone with a reason code and the retracting authority; hard deletion is permitted only where a legal or policy obligation requires it and is audited.

roles.name: Model owner
responsibilities: Own WM-XCT-008 in the adopting Dimension, approve version changes and adjudicate boundary disputes with sibling models.
Approve or reject adoption of value-affecting upstream registry changes.

roles.name: Unit registry steward
responsibilities: Maintain the pinned registry release manifest, the unit code crosswalk and the conversion factor table.
Reconcile upstream releases, classify changes, and issue deprecation and migration notices.
Review and retire local extension codes when upstream terms become available.

roles.name: Metrology reviewer
responsibilities: Review uncertainty statements for GUM conformance, including uncertainty type, coverage factor and coverage probability.
Approve conversion parameters, non-linear conversion functions and decision rules used for conformity assessment.
Challenge scale-type assignments and reject invalid arithmetic on interval and ordinal scales.

roles.name: Interoperability steward
responsibilities: Maintain the alignment and conflict register and the profile and value-set binding declarations.
Negotiate and record bindings with exchange partners, including non-conformance disposition.
Validate that a conformance claim is evidenced before it is published.

roles.name: Data protection and retention officer
responsibilities: Assign sensitivity classifications and retention rules to quantity values in host contexts.
Approve disclosure-control techniques such as precision reduction or banding and require them to be recorded as derivations.
Audit deletions, retractions and tombstones against policy.

access.default_rule: An embedded quantity value inherits the access rule of its host record; it has no independent access control surface. Where the host applies no explicit rule, the value defaults to the most restrictive classification available in the adopting Dimension until a classification is assigned.
exceptions: Unit, quantity kind and dimension metadata may be readable at a lower sensitivity than the numeric value, so that schema discovery and validation can operate without exposing values.

Precision-reduced or banded projections of a value may be released to a wider scope than the full-precision value, provided the transformation is recorded as a derivation and the recipient is told the value is derived.

Registry artifacts — crosswalks, conversion tables, release manifests, alignment registers — are ordinarily readable across the Dimension because they contain no subject data, unless a specific artifact encodes commercially sensitive process parameters.
Emergency or safety-critical reads may bypass a restrictive default under a break-glass procedure, which must be time-bounded, justified at the time of use and audited.
Uncertainty budgets and calibration evidence may be restricted more tightly than the values they substantiate where they disclose laboratory methods.
A conversion agent may read conversion-factor tables and unit vocabularies without access to host personal data.
Redacted original values remain visible to auditors for the retention period even when producers can no longer read them.
audit_requirements: Log every read of a full-precision value that crosses a sensitivity boundary, with the requesting identity, scope, purpose and an RFC 3339 timestamp.
Log every value-affecting write, conversion, rounding, retraction and disclosure-control application, retaining the prior value and the acting identity.
Log every registry release pin, reconciliation and migration notice issuance, with content digests and the change classification applied.
Retain audit entries at least as long as the values they describe, and independently of the value's own deletion, so that a deletion itself remains auditable.
Make audit entries queryable by unit code and by registry release so the blast radius of an upstream change can be established after the fact.
Record actor, event time, ingestion time, artefact identity and before/after version for conversion, policy change, deprecation and redaction.
Audit unknown-unit exceptions and refused conversions caused by kind mismatch or missing mapping.
