coverage.claim: A standards-led context structure for an embeddable Quantity/Unit value-object mixin, built on Claude's boundary set (BIPM SI Brochure 9th ed., JCGM VIM3 and GUM, ISO 80000-1:2022, CGPM 2022 Res 3, UCUM v2.2, UN/CEFACT Rec 20 Rev 17, QUDT v3.5.0, FHIR R5, D-SI v2.2.0, SOSA/SSN, RFC 3339, schema.org) and extended with three grok findings and three grok functions. Coverage is bounded to the value object: the measurement act, the measured thing, calendar identity, monetary amounts, calibration chains and domain property catalogues remain with sibling models, and ownership, access and retention stay declared evidence gaps rather than standards-derived content. No completeness across domains, jurisdictions or unit vocabularies is claimed, and no conformance to any cited standard is asserted.

checklist.notes: Unit identity is grounded in UCUM codes, UN/CEFACT common codes and QUDT IRIs with an explicit precedence rule, code-system version pinning and a case-sensitivity question. The value object itself deliberately has no independent identity: as an EMBED value object it inherits the host record's identity, which is stated explicitly in the embedding contract rather than left implicit.

Two distinct lifecycles are modelled and kept apart: the unit code's lifecycle in its upstream registry (active, deprecated, redefined, withdrawn, replaced, with successor and migration rule) and the recorded value's lifecycle (amended, superseded, retracted, tombstoned). QUDT v3.4.0/v3.5.0 breaking changes and the 2019 SI redefinition provide concrete primary evidence that this separation is necessary.

Relationships are covered through quantity-kind-to-unit applicability, commensurability and equality determinations, ratio numerator/denominator structure, logarithmic reference quantities, source-to-derived conversion links, supersession links, and fourteen composition links to sibling models and external vocabularies, each with mapping strength or relation type.

Event time and observation/ingestion time are modelled as separate fields, validity intervals and expiry are questioned, and RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated including preservation of '-00:00' for unknown local offset. Deeper calendar and interval semantics are explicitly delegated to the temporal sibling model.

Origin category, originating agent, derivation inputs, conversion provenance with explicit information-loss notes, registry release pinning with content digests, and traceability claims requiring cited calibration evidence. D-SI and SOSA support the delegation pattern used.

No consulted primary source assigns ownership or stewardship of a quantity value; metrology standards govern semantics, not custody. The registry entry itself records only 'owner designated by the adopting Dimension'. Ownership is therefore handled as a service-layer role definition and an explicit inheritance from the host record, and is marked a gap rather than presented as standards-backed.

Constraint specification (allowed unit value sets with binding strength, permitted value forms, plausibility ranges, cardinality, requiredness), scale-type operation restrictions, parser conformance levels, dimensional consistency checks, round-trip conversion checks, and re-evaluable validation outcomes pinned to registry versions. Supported by FHIR bindings, QUDT applicableUnit and UCUM conformance levels.

No primary metrology or units standard addresses access control for quantity values. Access is modelled as strictly inherited from the host record, with a most-restrictive default, exceptions for unit metadata and precision-reduced projections, and audit requirements. This is reasoned governance, not standards-derived normative content, and is marked a gap accordingly.

Likewise unsupported by any consulted primary source. The model states that an embedded value has no independent deletion lifecycle, that unit and provenance metadata may be retained after value deletion to keep remaining data interpretable, and that retraction leaves an audited tombstone — but these are policy positions of the adopting Dimension, not normative requirements.

Alignments to UCUM, UN/CEFACT Rec 20, QUDT, ISO 80000/SI, GUM, FHIR, schema.org and D-SI, each pinned by version and recorded with mapping strength, plus a conflict register, profile and value-set binding with declared non-conformance disposition, and an explicit rule that alignment never implies conformance.

Quantity kind, dimension, scale type (ratio, interval, ordinal, nominal), unit category (base, coherent derived, accepted for use with SI, off-system, customary, arbitrary, procedure-defined), value form and origin category are each modelled as governed classifications with authoritative sources.

Significant digits, trailing-zero preservation (grounded in FHIR's explicit rule that 0.010 differs from 0.01), exactness flags for defined values, mandated lossless numeric representation, and recorded rounding rules. This is the dimension most often lost in practice and is treated as semantic rather than implementational.

GUM-grounded uncertainty type, coverage factor and coverage probability, Type A versus Type B evaluation with evidence for Type B components, and a strict separation of measurement uncertainty from specification tolerance and from conformity decisions with their decision rules and guard bands.

Transport security, authentication and cryptographic controls are properties of the storage and interface projections, which this format-neutral mixin deliberately does not constrain. The one security-adjacent concern that genuinely belongs here — disclosure control by precision reduction changing the value's meaning — is modelled under access and disclosure.

known_omissions: Full normative text of ISO 80000-1:2022 and the other ISO 80000 parts is paywalled; only the public catalogue record (edition 2, December 2022) was read, so no clause-level claim is made against ISO 80000.

The SI Brochure and GUM were retrieved as PDFs that could not be machine-parsed in this session; their content is cited from the BIPM landing pages and from well-established published definitions, and clause-level quotation is not asserted for either.

Direct fetch of unece.org was blocked (HTTP 403) throughout; UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 Revision 17 (2021) and its three annexes were confirmed through the UNECE site's own indexed listings rather than by reading the page body.

VIM4 is in committee draft and may change definitions relied on here (notably around quantity, value and unit); this model is built against VIM3 (JCGM 200:2012) and will need re-checking on VIM4 publication.
No exhaustive unit atom inventory, prefix table or conversion factor set is reproduced; these belong in the pinned registry artifacts, not in the model.
Statistical uncertainty propagation methods, including the GUM Supplement 1 Monte Carlo approach, are referenced only as an extension point and are not modelled.
Legal metrology requirements — trade approval, verification marks, national weights-and-measures law — are not covered and are jurisdiction-specific.
Sexagesimal, fractional-inch and other non-decimal customary presentations are acknowledged only through the presentation finding; no normalisation rules are specified.

The Ontology of units of Measure (OM 2) could not be retrieved (TLS certificate mismatch on its published host) and is therefore absent from the alignment set despite being a credible sibling vocabulary.
Full text of ISO 80000-1:2022 and ISO 11240:2012 is paywalled; abstracts and public tables of contents were used, so clause-level data-element names from those standards may be incomplete.
UCUM 2.2 prefix table as published 2024-06-17 does not show ronna, quetta, ronto or quecto; whether a later UCUM revision added them was not verified beyond this version.
OIML legal-metrology instruments, WELMEC guides and national weights-and-measures statutes were not taken as primary sources.
Digital calibration certificate (DCC) schemas, CODATA least-squares constant adjustments after 2019, and VIM4 draft revisions are not incorporated.
IEC 80000-13 information-science units, UDUNITS, OM ontology, SensorML/SWE Quantity, UN/CEFACT CCTS Quantity.Type and schema.org QuantitativeValue are discovery alignments only.
Vector, tensor, complex, distributional and interval-arithmetic quantity types beyond FHIR Range are not modelled.
Catalytic enzyme units, WHO International Units and other biological potency systems are covered only as arbitrary/procedure-defined units.
conflicts: schema.org documents currency codes such as USD as valid unitCode values alongside physical unit codes, although a currency has no quantity dimension and cannot participate in dimensional analysis. This model refuses that conflation and routes monetary amounts to a Money sibling.

QUDT v3.5.0 redefined BIT, BYTE and OCTET as counting/storage units rather than information-entropy units, and v3.4.0 replaced ambiguous skos:broader use with an explicit commensurability framework. Values recorded against earlier releases may carry different semantics, which is why release pinning is mandatory here.

UCUM full conformance requires recognising that 'km' equals '1000.m', while limited conformance permits literal string comparison. Two systems can both claim UCUM support and still disagree on equality, so the conformance level must be declared per deployment.

UCUM annotations in curly braces must be discarded by fully conformant parsers, yet they are widely used in practice to carry denominator or specimen meaning. Any semantics placed there is unreliable and must be relocated to structured fields.

NIST SP 811 (2008) has not been updated for the 2019 SI revision and NIST itself redirects users to SP 330 (2019); style and conversion guidance therefore requires explicit edition pinning rather than generic citation.

VIM 1.9 records that units with the same dimension may denote different kinds (hertz for frequency, becquerel for activity, both 1/s; joule per kelvin for both heat capacity and entropy), so dimension-based equivalence used by many implementations is demonstrably unsafe.

UN/CEFACT Rec 20 common codes and UCUM expressions are not in one-to-one correspondence: some trade codes are packaging or commercial units with no metrological unit equivalent, so crosswalk rows require explicit mapping strength rather than assumed equality.

UCUM defining bases (metre, second, gram, radian, kelvin, coulomb, candela) are not isomorphic with SI bases; mole is a count in UCUM and radian is a base, whereas SI treats the radian as a dimensionless derived unit.
NIST SP 811 Appendix A still states pre-2019 artefact-based base-unit definitions and the publication itself warns it has not been updated for the 2019 SI.
SI Brochure guidance after version 3.01 urges explicit units for quantities of dimension one, which conflicts with widespread practice of omitting the unit one.
Gray versus sievert and joule versus newton metre share dimensions but not quantity kinds; dimension-only converters will silently mis-convert.
UNECE Rec 20 tabulated three-character codes cannot express arbitrary UCUM products, so trade and scientific unit languages are not 1:1.
FHIR treats Money as distinct from Quantity, while QUDT includes CurrencyUnit in the same schema family.
Degree Celsius is an SI unit that is incoherent with the SI in UCUM special-unit semantics; prefixing Celsius scales the numerical value, not a ratio-scale unit.
regional_assumptions: The SI is assumed as the reference system, with customary and off-system units treated as convertible alternatives. Jurisdictions with statutory customary-unit requirements will need a locally bound presentation and storage policy.
UN/CEFACT Rec 20 is assumed as the trade code list. Domain-specific regimes (for example customs tariff schedules or sector-specific code lists) may mandate different codes in the same exchange.

UCUM is assumed as the machine grammar, reflecting its adoption in healthcare through FHIR; other sectors may mandate a different expression syntax, in which case the parser conformance declaration must name it.
Decimal separators, digit grouping and unit name spelling vary by locale and language; the model treats these as presentation concerns bound to a pinned style authority rather than as data.

Access, disclosure and retention positions assume a general-purpose governance regime; jurisdictions with specific data protection, health, financial or trade-secret statutes will impose stricter rules that override the defaults here.

Calendar-dependent duration units such as month and year are ambiguous across contexts; FHIR's practice of treating 'mo' as a calendar month when calculating recurrence is one convention among several and must be declared per deployment.
SI is treated as the default physical system of units; US customary and Imperial units are supported only as named non-SI systems with explicit variants such as US versus Imperial gallon.
English and French names in the SI Brochure are both authentic; this research used English texts.
UNECE Rec 20 is assumed for international trade EDI; some jurisdictions mandate additional national unit lists that were not reviewed.
ISO 11240 is global IDMP but operationally driven by medicines regulators; non-health Dimensions may ignore it without losing SI alignment.
NIST SP 811 informs US style and conversion rounding but is not a substitute for the current SI Brochure.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample to dimension-based comparability: hertz and becquerel are both 1/s and joule per kelvin serves both heat capacity and entropy (VIM 1.9 Note 2), so any structure that treated dimension equality as sufficient for comparison was rejected; quantity-kind agreement is required as a separate test.

Counterexample to uniform conversion: degree Celsius is a special unit on a non-ratio scale (UCUM), and converting a temperature difference differs from converting a temperature point. A single multiplier-and-offset conversion function was rejected in favour of an explicit point-or-difference designation.

Counterexample to unit universality: UCUM states that arbitrary units carry no general meaning relative to any other unit and form no equivalence classes. Rather than warn and approximate, the model requires outright refusal of such comparisons — a stricter position than most implementations take.

Counterexample to precision as an implementation detail: FHIR states explicitly that 0.010 differs from 0.01 and that original precision must be preserved. Any structure that allowed numeric normalisation through binary floating point was rejected, and numeric representation was elevated to a semantic policy.

Counterexample to registry stability: QUDT reclassified BIT, BYTE and OCTET between v3.4.0 and v3.5.0, and CGPM extended the prefix set in 2022. A design that resolved units against a floating 'latest' vocabulary was rejected in favour of mandatory release pinning with content digests.

Rejected attractive structure — a Measurement or Observation bundle: SOSA/SSN is a W3C Recommendation that already models the observing act and explicitly delegates unit encoding, so adding sensors, procedures or features of interest here would have duplicated a sibling model and violated the registry's EMBED value-object constraint.

Rejected attractive structure — a Currency or Money bundle: although schema.org places currency codes in unitCode and FHIR defines MoneyQuantity, a currency has no dimension and cannot be dimensionally analysed. Including it would have imported foreign-exchange, rounding-to-minor-unit and legal-tender concerns with no metrological basis.

Rejected attractive structure — a unit registry curation bundle: publication cadence, code issuance and deprecation policy for UCUM, Rec 20 and QUDT are owned by their issuing organisations. This model consumes and pins those releases; asserting curation authority over them would have been unsupportable.

Tested the mandatory field set against D-SI v2.2.0, which carries value, unit and uncertainty as one payload: the resulting embedding contract requires value plus reference as an atomic pair, with uncertainty conditionally required, rather than treating uncertainty as an optional afterthought.

Checked whether ownership, access and retention could be grounded in any consulted primary source. They could not, so all three are marked as gaps in the checklist and handled as explicit inheritance from the host record rather than dressed up as standards-derived requirements.
If an agent converts gray to sievert or joule to newton metre because the dimension vectors match, the model has failed the kind-mismatch constraint.
If an agent applies a 273.15 offset to a temperature interval marked as a delta, conversion is wrong.
If an agent treats a UCUM curly-brace annotation as a unit, or treats {RBC} as commensurable with 1, semantic comparison is wrong.
If an agent deletes a deprecated unit so that a historical millimetre-of-mercury value can no longer be interpreted, retention policy is violated.
If an agent claims SI conformance while storing UCUM radian as an independent base without recording the non-isomorphism, the alignment has been over-claimed.
If a currency amount is stored as a Quantity with system ISO 4217 instead of being redirected to a money sibling, scope has been breached.
If conversion overwrites the original lexical decimal 0.010 to 0.01, presentation precision required by FHIR decimal has been lost.
